objective: Three standalone modules for Typeless-style 'auto dictionary', 'interaction sounds' and 'mute other audio while dictating', each with tests, without touching desktop.py. (1) voice2txt/learning.py (pure): `candidates(original_segments, edited_text, known_terms)` compares the concatenated model output against the user's edited text with difflib (token level: CJK runs split into characters, latin words kept) and returns a list of {'term', 'replaced', 'count'} where term is a replacement of 1–6 CJK chars or a latin word/phrase up to 3 words that (a) is not in known_terms, (b) is not pure punctuation/digits, (c) differs from the replaced token; capitalised latin words and CJK runs that replace similar-length runs rank first; dedupe and count repeats across segments; `merge_vocabulary(manual, accepted_auto)` returns the comma-joined glossary with manual first, max 1000 chars. (2) voice2txt/sounds.py: generate two short tones with the stdlib `wave` module at first use into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voice2Txt\sounds (start: 880 Hz 90 ms with 10 ms fades; stop: 660 Hz 90 ms; error: 330 Hz 150 ms) and play them with winsound.PlaySound(path, SND_FILENAME|SND_ASYNC|SND_NODEFAULT); `play(name, enabled=True)` never raises; the generator is a pure function returning bytes that tests can validate (RIFF header, sample count). (3) voice2txt/audiofocus.py (Win32 Core Audio via ctypes COM, no comtypes/pycaw): `mute_others(own_pid)` enumerates the default render endpoint's audio sessions (CoInitialize, CoCreateInstance MMDeviceEnumerator, GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eConsole), Activate IAudioSessionManager2, GetSessionEnumerator, for each session QueryInterface IAudioSessionControl2 -> GetProcessId, skip own pid and system sounds session, QueryInterface ISimpleAudioVolume -> GetMute/SetMute) and returns a handle listing the sessions it muted (only those that were not already muted); `restore(handle)` unmutes exactly those; register an atexit restore and make restore idempotent; all failures are swallowed into handle.errors so the app never breaks because of audio. Define GUIDs/vtable offsets as constants with comments naming the interface methods. (4) tests/test_learning_sounds.py: learning candidates (CJK replacement, latin proper noun, ignores punctuation/digits, respects known_terms, counts repeats, merge_vocabulary order and cap) and sounds generator validity (parse with wave module, duration ±5 ms). (5) scripts/check_audiofocus.py: real check: start a helper python child that loops winsound.PlaySound on a generated silent-ish 1 s wav (SND_LOOP|SND_ASYNC) so an audio session exists, call mute_others, assert via GetMute that the child's session is muted and our own is not in the handle, restore, assert unmuted, terminate the child; writes verification/audiofocus-2026-11-13.json with ok=true, sessions_seen, muted_pids.
acceptance: `.\.build-venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -v` passes with at least 8 new tests, none touching audio devices or COM.
`scripts\check_audiofocus.py` writes ok=true: the helper's session was found, muted (GetMute TRUE), then restored (GetMute FALSE); own pid never muted; no python child left running.
`python -c "from voice2txt import sounds; sounds.play('start'); sounds.play('stop')"` exits 0 (audible tones acceptable) and the two wav files exist under the LOCALAPPDATA sounds folder.
notes: Do NOT edit desktop.py or any existing module. The check script will briefly play a quiet looping sound; keep it short (<5 s). Do not run git.
